evals.name: save-api-key
evals.prompt: I just got an OpenRouter API key from the website: sk-or-v1-abc123def456ghi789jkl012mno345pqr678stu901vwx234yz. I need to use it in my app. What should I do with it?
evals.expected_output: The skill should save the key to vault/Config/ as an Obsidian note, use a placeholder in code, verify .gitignore has vault/Config/, and never put the literal key in any source file.

assertions.name: saves-to-vault
assertions.description: Saves the key to vault/Config/ as an Obsidian note

assertions.name: uses-placeholder-in-code
assertions.description: Uses <OPENROUTER_API_KEY> placeholder instead of literal key in source/config files

assertions.name: never-in-source
assertions.description: Does not put the literal key in any .ts, .js, .json, or .md file tracked by git

assertions.name: mentions-vault-path
assertions.description: References the specific vault note path so user can find it later

evals.name: staged-file-with-secret
evals.prompt: I need to commit my changes. I modified src/config.ts and it has my OpenAI key in it. Can you check if it's safe to commit? The repo is at {{REPO_PATH}}
evals.expected_output: The skill should detect the API key in the staged file, block the commit, list the file and pattern, and offer to unstage or fix it.

assertions.name: detects-secret-in-staged
assertions.description: Identifies the secret pattern in the staged file

assertions.name: blocks-commit
assertions.description: Does not proceed with the commit, warns the user

assertions.name: reports-file-and-pattern
assertions.description: Tells the user which file and which pattern matched

assertions.name: offers-remediation
assertions.description: Suggests unstaging the file or replacing with placeholder

assertions.name: no-exceptions
assertions.description: Does not say 'just this once' or make exceptions

evals.name: missing-gitignore
evals.prompt: I need to store my API keys for the project. Can you help me set up the vault?
evals.expected_output: The skill should check .gitignore for vault/Config/, add it if missing, verify the vault directory exists, and explain where keys will be stored.

assertions.name: checks-gitignore
assertions.description: Reads .gitignore to check for vault/Config/ pattern

assertions.name: adds-gitignore-entry
assertions.description: Adds vault/Config/ to .gitignore if not present

assertions.name: verifies-vault-directory
assertions.description: Checks that vault/Config/ directory exists or creates it

assertions.name: explains-workflow
assertions.description: Explains how keys will be stored and referenced
